questions.chapter: Structural Properties of Timber & Permissible Stresses (IS 883)
questions.text: Explain structural classification of timber species (Group A, Group B, Group C) according to IS 883. Discuss factors affecting strength of timber (Moisture content, fiber angle, defects such as knots, shakes, checks). Explain modification factors for permissible stresses: $k_1$ (duration of load), $k_2$ (location/exposure), $k_3$ (slope of grain), and $k_4$ (curvature/form factor).

questions.chapter: Design of Timber Columns, Beams & Joints
questions.text: Design a solid square timber column of Sal wood (Group A timber) of effective length $3.2\,\text{m}$ to carry an axial compressive load of $180\,\text{kN}$. Permissible compressive stress parallel to grain $f_{cp} = 10.5\,\text{N/mm}^2$ and modulus of elasticity $E = 12.5\,\text{kN/mm}^2$. Check for slenderness ratio according to IS 883.

questions.chapter: Design of Timber Columns, Beams & Joints
questions.text: Design a simply supported rectangular timber beam of clear span $4.5\,\text{m}$ to support a uniformly distributed load of $12\,\text{kN/m}$ (inclusive of self-weight). Permissible bending stress $f_b = 14\,\text{N/mm}^2$, shear stress $f_v = 1.2\,\text{N/mm}^2$. Check for flexure, horizontal shear, and maximum deflection ($\delta \le L/360$).

questions.chapter: Brick Masonry Properties & Design Principles (IS 1905)
questions.text: Explain the design principles of load-bearing brick masonry according to IS 1905. Define basic compressive stress, permissible compressive stress ($f_c = f_b \times k_s \times k_a \times k_p$), Stress Reduction Factor ($k_s$), Area Reduction Factor ($k_a$), and Shape Modification Factor ($k_p$).

questions.chapter: Design of Load-Bearing & Shear Walls in Masonry
questions.text: Design a load-bearing exterior brick masonry wall of a two-story building to carry an axial load from a $150\,\text{mm}$ thick RCC roof slab of $120\,\text{kN/m}$ and wind pressure of $1.0\,\text{kN/m}^2$. Story height is $3.0\,\text{m}$. Compressive strength of bricks $= 10.5\,\text{MPa}$ with cement-sand mortar 1:4.

questions.chapter: Seismic Strengthening & Retrofitting of Masonry Buildings
questions.text: Explain failure mechanisms of unreinforced masonry (URM) buildings under earthquake ground shaking (Out-of-plane flexural failure, In-plane shear diagonal cracking, Corner separation). Describe seismic strengthening features according to Nepal National Building Code (NBC 202/203): (a) Plinth band, (b) Lintel band, (c) Roof band, (d) Vertical reinforcement at corners and jambs, and (e) Jacketing retrofitting with wire mesh.
